title: Finn and the Wobbly Stairs
markdown:
Every school has its own special something, and Oakhaven School had a very special something indeed. It wasn't the wonky clock in the hall, or the slightly lopsided gingerbread man that sat on Mrs. Gable’s desk, which always looked like it had a stubbed toe. Oh no. It was the staircase.

This wasn't just any staircase. This was Finn's staircase. Finn the stairkeeper. He wasn't a keeper of keys, or a keeper of secrets, but a keeper of stairs. And these stairs… well, they had a mind of their own. They were grand and made of polished oak, but they were also rather spirited. They’d stretch and shrink, twist and turn, all on their own schedule. It was Finn’s job to make sure everyone got where they were going, even if ‘where they were going’ changed every five minutes.

His friend, Whisper, a stair sprite no bigger than a robin, would flit about, her wings a shimmer of moonlight and dewdrop. She was quick as a wink and always full of fun. "Finn, my dear fellow!" she'd chirrup, her voice like tinkling bells in a gentle breeze. "Another glorious morning for the Oakhaven Oscillations! Are the steps feeling particularly springy today?"

And indeed, they were. As the first bell rang, a soft thump-wobble-jiggle would echo through the school, a sound as familiar to the children as the rustle of turning pages. The grand staircase, which usually led from the dusty ground floor to the cheerful first floor, would shift. One minute it was there, a solid pathway to learning, the next, poof! It would be snaking its way with a whoosh and a sigh towards the art room, its colourful paintings beckoning.

Finn would just sigh, a puff of air that ruffled his sandy hair, and with his trusty (and slightly squeaky) mop, he'd guide the children safely. "Mind the sway, little ones! Hold on tight! This way to history!" he’d call out, his brow furrowed in concentration.

Whisper would giggle, darting ahead like a shimmering dragonfly. "This way to adventure, you mean!" she'd chirp, her laughter echoing like tiny wind chimes.

But one Tuesday, as the third bell chimed its cheerful tune, signalling the start of lessons, the staircase did its usual jig. Only this time, it didn't quite finish. It wobbled, it jiggled with extra vigour, and then… it stopped, halfway up, with its top landing smack-dab outside the attic observatory door. And all the children who had been climbing it at the time? Poof! Some were tucked into dusty broom cupboards, others peered with wide eyes from behind forgotten gym mats, and a whole class of Year Fours found themselves having an impromptu lesson in the stationery cupboard, surrounded by reams of paper and boxes of pencils.

"Oh dear," whispered Finn, his brow furrowed like a crumpled map. His heart gave a little thump. This was a bigger jiggle than usual.

Suddenly, a voice boomed from the school intercom, its tone like a grumpy badger waking from a nap. It was the Headteacher, Mrs. Prickleworthy, and her voice sounded like a kettle that had forgotten to whistle. "Attention, students and staff! Due to an unexpected structural anomaly with our main staircase, all classes will proceed with extreme caution. Finn, Mr. Finn, report to my office immediately!"

Ah, but here's the thing. Finn and Whisper were already on the moving staircase, stranded halfway to nowhere. And if they went back down, they might miss their chance to help. The usual path was gone, vanished into the school’s peculiar architecture.

Finn’s knees started to feel like jelly that had been left out in the sun. He looked up. Up, up, up, to the tiny, round door of the attic observatory. It seemed miles away, a distant star in a sky of plaster and beams. A little tremor rippled through his arms, making his mop twitch. This is too high, he thought, his breath catching in his throat like a tiny bird trapped in a cage. His palms felt clammy.

"We have to get to the attic!" Whisper declared, her tiny voice surprisingly firm, like a determined little drumbeat. She zipped in front of Finn’s nose, her wings buzzing with purpose. "That’s where the Great Gear is. It controls the staircase’s final landing. If we can set it right, everyone will be free!"

Finn hesitated. He looked at the steep incline ahead, the way the stairs were angled like a slippery slide. He thought about turning back, heading for the comforting, if currently absent, ground floor. It would be so much easier to just… not. But then he imagined the Year Fours, giggling amongst the paper. He imagined the children in the broom cupboards, their faces pale. "Alright," he said, taking a deep, shaky breath that tasted of dust. "Alright. For them."

And wouldn't you know it, as Finn took that first brave step onto the steeply angled stairs, something changed. The sway felt less sway-like. The steepness seemed less steep. He focused on Whisper, on the mission, and on the thought of all the happy, relieved faces he would see when they were safe. His tummy butterflies seemed to calm their wings a little.

They reached the attic door. With a firm shove, Finn pushed it open, his heart thumping a steady rhythm now. Inside, a huge, whirring contraption of gears and levers sat humming softly, like a contented, mechanical giant. This was the Great Gear, the heart of the staircase’s magic. It was made of brass and iron, with shiny cogs and sturdy wheels.

"Quick, Finn!" Whisper urged, her wings a blur of excitement. "You have to turn it to the 'Settled' position! That will tell the stairs to be still!"

Finn’s hands were still a bit shaky, but he moved with a new purpose. He grasped the largest lever, its metal cool and smooth under his fingers. He had to leave his special, squeaky mop behind on a dusty ledge to get a better grip. He pulled it down with all his might, hearing a satisfying clunk that echoed through the attic. The entire staircase outside the window gave a final, gentle shudder, like a sleeping cat stretching, and settled into its usual place, leading right to the ground floor. A sigh of relief seemed to ripple through the old building.

Just then, the attic door burst open with a bang that made Finn jump slightly. Mrs. Prickleworthy stood there, her sensible shoes planted firmly on the floor, her face a mixture of relief and bewilderment. "Finn! Whisper! What in the name of all that is orderly are you doing up here? And why is the main staircase behaving so… cooperatively?"

Then she looked out the window. The staircase was fixed. And all the children, who had been peeking out from their various hiding spots, began to cheer, their voices rising in a happy wave.

Finn, standing tall, no longer felt the flutter of butterflies in his tummy. He felt a warm glow spreading through him, like sunshine on a chilly morning. He had done it. He had faced his fear and helped everyone. He even managed a small, confident smile.

"We… we just made sure everything was… settled, Headteacher," Finn said, his voice clear and steady.

Whisper winked from Finn’s shoulder, her eyes sparkling. "That's the curious thing about stairkeepers," she chirped, her voice full of mischief. "They always make sure things end up in the right place, even when they're a bit wobbly!"

As the happy, relieved children poured down the newly stable staircase, their laughter echoing through the halls, a little step ahead of them gave a tiny, almost imperceptible shimmy. Finn, without even thinking, reached out and steadied himself with a calm hand. He looked at the staircase, then at Whisper, a knowing twinkle in his eye. It was just a little wobble, and he was ready for anything.
characters: Finn the stairkeeper, Whisper the stair sprite
